blocks.text: Real-world basis: Lenticular clouds, aurora curtains, mirages, folded-paper landscapes, and visible weather fronts.

Landscape: The seam of an Era Two world fold remains visible across the sky. On one side, mountains obey one atmospheric law; on the other, plains use another. The boundary migrates slowly across the ground.

Mini timeline: Era Two — Two failing environments are joined so that each can supply a missing keystone process. The join is functional but never fully hidden. Era Three — Settlements track the seam because food, gravity, sound, and weather change as it passes. Some communities follow it; others build heavy anchor architecture to resist it.
Present condition: Stable as a moving boundary, unstable for fixed settlements.

Aesthetic brief: A visible crease or aurora-like plane crossing sky and land. Clouds, stars, color temperature, and distant perspective differ on each side. The foreground can show a tree with leaves governed by one side and roots by the other.
Background profile: Variable; composite boundary biome; awe-filled, hazardous, migratory; friction can shift when the seam passes.
